newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil keeps mum on potential cost of pay ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil keeps mum on potential cost of pay ruling.

text.p: The Brazilian government has not yet calculated how a 28.9 percent pay rise awarded to 11 civil servants might affect public finances if extended to all the federal workforce, a Finance Ministry spokesman said.

"This decision affects only the 11 and anything else is speculation," the spokesman said. "Of course the government has to take steps to protect itself but it's not going to comment on something that hasn't happened."

The Supreme Federal Tribunal Wednesday ruled in favor of the civil servants in a controversial decision which the government fears is likely to set a precedent for the federal government's 500,000 workers and a similar number of pensioners.
The 11 successfully claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent pay rise issued to the armed forces in 1993, during the presidency of Itamar Franco.
Newspapers have estimated the decision might cost the government $20 billion in backdated pay plus $7.0 billion this year, a severe blow to its attempts to rein in public spending.
